label: Dense positional: first ~4 input steps and the whole copy phase
explanation: A broad, dense feature (active on about 72% of all steps) that tracks position. It fires on the first four original-input steps (100% at t=0, then falling to about 62% at t=3) and on nearly every copy-phase step after the delimiter (about 94%). It is mostly silent at the <DEL> step (18%) and at later original-phase positions (orig_idx 4-8, rate dropping to 12-47%). Magnitude: the largest activations are early in the input phase (t=1-3), and the inputs p, q and f boost them; the top examples all begin q p p, peaking on the second p. Copy-phase activations are moderate and fairly uniform across recall_idx. Output token, first token, digit count and whether the copy is correct have little effect. Misses are mostly weak activations at original positions 4-6; false positives are mostly near-zero steps late in the input or at the end of the copy.

issues: Most factual claims hold on dev. Overall active rate is 72.3%. By t, the rate is 1.00, 0.89, 0.74, 0.62 for t=0-3. Copy phase is 94.1%, the <DEL> step 18.5%, and orig_idx 4-8 falls from 0.465 to 0.121. The top examples all begin q p p and peak on the second p. Original test scores reproduce: P 0.887, R 0.897, F1 0.892, mass recall 0.916.

Systematic miss class that the predicate leaves out: inputs p, q and f at late original positions (phase 0, t>=4). Active rates there are p 0.985, q 0.931 and f 0.779 (combined 0.899), against 0.15-0.35 for most other letters. u (0.54), 1 (0.48) and 3 (0.47) are also elevated. The explanation names p/q/f only as magnitude boosters. It says misses are 'mostly weak activations at original positions 4-6', but in fact a clear token class at those positions fires almost every time.

There is also a carry-over effect: after a p/q/f input in late original positions, a non-p/q/f token fires about 65% of the time. In the misses output, late original-phase activations often trail off after a strong earlier activation.

Smaller points that don't change the picture. At the <DEL> step the feature fires about 41% of the time when L<=4 (54% when L=3), versus 18% overall, so <DEL> is not uniformly silent. Copy-phase rates are flat at about 0.90-0.97 across recall_idx, which matches the explanation.

The label 'first ~4 input steps' is a soft cutoff. The rate declines smoothly (t=2: 0.74, t=3: 0.62, t=4: 0.47), and t<3 gives dev F1 0.873 versus 0.892 for t<4. The label slightly overstates the step at t=4, but this is minor.
